items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Oh, near Buffao. [INTERVIEWEE] Near Buffalo, where I grew up.

ctx.x: those, and then he gave me “The Well Tempered Clavier,” and then I remember Emerson, Lake and Palmer came out with “Pictures at an Exhibition,” and it had probably been out for a while but, you know, it was a record club thing. I think I bought “Tarkus” was their first record, because it had a little giant armadillo on it and I thought, oh that’s a cool cover. And I just bought it because of the cover, and loved the music and then bought all their other records. So I discovered “Pictures at an Exhibition” and I…

Near Buffalo, where I grew up. And so I brought this piece in and he goes, “you know that’s a piano piece.” And I go, “it is?” You know, I had no clue. And he was really nice. He bought me the music so I started learning that, and then, you know I’d practice all the time and my chops were really getting strong on my own.
